output_json.patch_notes:
1) tapestry-ioc AbstractResource.forFile(String relativePath): normalize the untrusted relativePath with `relativePath.replace('\\', '/')` before `split("/")`, so backslash-separated '..' segments are collapsed/bounds-checked by the existing logic exactly like forward-slash segments (throwing IllegalStateException if they'd escape above the resource root), instead of being appended as one opaque, unresolved path term. This is the shared root-cause fix at the trust boundary named in the alert (AbstractResource.forFile), and applies to every caller of forFile, not just the context-asset handler.
2) tapestry-core ContextAssetRequestHandler.handleAssetRequest(): kept the existing cheap raw-prefix blacklist check (unchanged, preserves the existing unit test that passes a null rootContextResource), and added a second check of the same `illegal` pattern against the *resolved* `resource.getPath()` returned by `forFile()`, after '.' / '..' segments and separator variants have been normalized. This closes the "foo/../WEB-INF/..." (and backslash-equivalent) bypass of the WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml blacklist, which worked even without any backslash involvement since the original check only ever looked at the raw, un-resolved extraPath.
3) Added ContextAssetRequestHandlerTest.ensure_dot_dot_and_backslash_bypasses_of_blacklist_are_rejected, a data-provider test covering forward-slash "..", double "..", and backslash-separator variants that resolve into WEB-INF, verifying they're all rejected. Verified this fails on the pre-patch code (path reaches the resource-streaming call instead of being rejected) and passes post-patch.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The forFile() change is a pure normalization added before existing logic — legitimate forward-slash-only relative paths (the vast majority of real usage) are completely unaffected since replace('\\','/') is a no-op for them; only paths containing backslashes change behavior (they're now treated as separators, matching how '/' was already handled, and matching how the underlying OS/servlet container would ultimately interpret them anyway on Windows). The ContextAssetRequestHandler change is additive (a second check after resolving the resource) and does not alter behavior for previously-legitimate, non-malicious asset requests — those resolve to a resource.getPath() outside the WEB-INF/META-INF/*.tml blacklist and stream exactly as before. Confirmed :tapestry-ioc and :tapestry-core (main + test) compile cleanly, and the new/existing tests in ContextAssetRequestHandlerTest all pass (8/8, ran via a scoped TestNG suite since the project's Gradle task filters TestNG by suite file rather than --tests). Note: a full `./gradlew test` run in this environment separately fails on an unrelated, pre-existing issue (ResponseCompressionAnalyzerTest fails to load with a "ClassFormatError: Illegal method name" from a stale/incompatible Spock-compiled test class) — verified this reproduces identically on the unmodified baseline via git stash, so it is unrelated to and unaffected by this patch.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path traversal in the context-asset request path (ContextAssetRequestHandler → ChecksumPath → AbstractResource.forFile → ContextResource → ContextImpl.getRealFile). AbstractResource.forFile() only split relative paths on '/', so a backslash-separated segment such as "..\..\..\WEB-INF\web.xml" was treated as a single opaque path term instead of being collapsed by the existing "." / ".." bounds-checking logic, and was passed through largely unnormalized to the servlet container's getRealPath()/File resolution — which (notably on Windows) interprets backslashes as real separators, allowing escape outside the context root or reach into WEB-INF/META-INF. Separately, ContextAssetRequestHandler's WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml blacklist only checked the raw, un-resolved extraPath, so a value like "foo/../WEB-INF/web.xml" (or the backslash equivalent) bypassed the prefix check entirely since it doesn't start with "WEB-INF" until resolved.
